findings.impact: A malicious or unexpected commit can disclose or modify local data, and untracked external inputs can make a conservative report unsound.
findings.text: The commit-only design permits materializing Git tree entries while preserving modes but does not constrain symlink dereferencing or filesystem containment. A committed source symlink to an absolute or parent-relative path can make a naive analyzer read outside the claimed snapshot (including private local files) or let materialization/write/cleanup escape the temporary root; external target bytes also are not covered by the snapshot identity. Require safe no-follow or proven contained, explicitly pinned resolution and unbounded gaps when link dependencies cannot be modeled; protect writes and cleanup, and test absolute/relative/link-chain escapes against external sentinels.

output.summary: Committed-snapshot symlink containment is specified and the prior finding is resolved.
Approved portable commit-only analysis and committed symlink handling.

responses.adversary_design:5:1: fixed: Define no-follow or same-tree proven link resolution, unbounded fallback for unsupported or escaping dependencies, root-contained creation and cleanup, and sentinel tests for absolute, relative and chained escapes.

output.summary: Require safe handling of committed symlinks and root-contained materialization, with conservative gaps where link dependencies cannot be proven inside the pinned tree. Add escape, link-chain and cleanup tests without changing the portable commit-only scope.
Both reviews approve the committed-snapshot symlink and containment boundaries; the prior finding is resolved. No open findings or notes require verdicts.

blocked.instructions: Checkpoint 9e5b0af adds conservative cross-file typed-receiver hierarchy candidates: all explicit class-name candidates, raw extends/implements links in both directions without hop limits, and candidate method overloads/overrides are retained as inferred possibilities. Source identities remain ambiguous and the existing global full fallback remains mandatory. Three new tests pass including a real Git/CLI scenario; the five previous candidate tests, 15 CLI contract tests, 27 coordinator tests and npm run build pass. Continue implementation: (1) successfully validate a coherent production worktree snapshot backend for ordinary checkouts or use a suitable supported environment; this host uses root-owned /home Btrfs subvolume, the repository is not a subvolume and user_subvol_rm_allowed is absent. Do not use best-effort watchers or before/after hashes as proof. (2) extend cross-file module/type bindings, callbacks, inheritance and language coverage with justified candidates and explicit uncertainty. (3) define a defensible supported-model completeness criterion before removing unconditional fallback for nonempty trees, and test end-to-end. This checkpoint is partial and not a complete sparse analyzer.

spec: Implement conservative impact analysis directly in this Trail-code fork specified in docs/test-impact/design.md, sections 1–6, 8, 11–13 and delivery steps 1–2. Use upstream base ca20a67764e99531a1cf272eea8354e2c16f71d9 and define versioned impact contracts and exact explicit endpoints. Analyze both snapshots, preserve ambiguity and analysis gaps, traverse complete reverse dependencies without arbitrary limits, handle deletions, renames and rebinding, and isolate and validate conservative caches. Report justified fallback scopes instead of silently omitting uncertainty. Include meaningful tests for endpoint semantics, graph completeness, gaps, cache freshness and representative dependency cases. Preserve upstream licensing and document the pinned source. Do not implement a replacement parser or assume normal navigation output is conservative. The full design and its acceptance matrix are binding; resolve open distribution and interface choices through the workflow. Work directly in this fork for a future upstream pull request; no separate test-impact repository or Git subtree. Preserve the separate Unity plugin branch. Where the design refers to a separate fork and adapter distribution, adapt it to this unified repository. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
